class: Discovery guarded and registered applications against SQLite while runs and the dashboard track in Postgres, so submitted postings re-queued as ghost rows and the status script reported the shadow as pending
fix: queue_discovered_job, scan ingest, and get_discovered_jobs consult the live tracker (tracking.open_tracker) for the submitted cover and register through tracker.create/update_status under the run's URL-hash key; agent_status reads the live tracker with a stale-labelled SQLite fallback; scripts/rekey_f329.py unified the five already-queued shadow rows onto URL keys (run 3 Nov, backup kept). Tests run TRACKER=sqlite by default (tests/conftest.py) so none touches the owner's Postgres.
prevention: Application state is read and written only through tracking.open_tracker; the feed file's applications table is never consulted, and status tooling reads the same tracker the dashboard does.
root_cause: The October SQLite-to-Postgres move left discovery behind: queue_discovered_job's already-submitted guard and registration, scan_all's ingest status, and get_discovered_jobs' hide_applied filter all read the feed file's applications table, which runs never write. Submitted postings (Fastly, Verizon, Rackspace, Roblox, Analog -- all decided in Postgres) re-queued as ready_to_apply ghosts, and agent_status.py's direct SQLite read reported six pendings while Postgres held one. Queueing also keyed rows by the discovery hash instead of the run's URL hash.
site: Discovery-to-application handoff, job_discovery.py + tracking.py + scripts/agent_status.py + tests/conftest.py, 3 November 2026
symptom: Five submitted-or-live postings sat as ready_to_apply ghosts in data/applications.db while the live tracker showed them submitted (and Analog needing review); every new scan or Apply could re-queue a submitted posting, and the multi-agent status script disagreed with the dashboard.
why_tests_missed: Feed tests hand-built a minimal applications table in the same temp file, so the guard and the registration trivially agreed; no test separated the feed file from the applications tracker, and none ran with Postgres configured.
